newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala adopts lethal injection for executions.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala adopts lethal injection for executions.

text.p: Six weeks after media images of a gruesome firing squad execution saturated Guatemala congress has passed a law to change the method of execution to lethal injection, an official said on Thursday.
"It was passed unanimously" Jorge Mario Salguero, congressional spokesman, told Reuters.

The method of execution generated controversy after two convicts, blindfolded and bound in front of a dirt wall, were not killed by the initial rifle shots, forcing an army officer to kill them with a pistol shot to their heads.
Children were exposed to graphic newspaper and television coverage of the execution of the two men, who were convicted of raping and murdering a four-year-old girl.
The president of congress, Carlos Garcia Regas, presented the law in early October as a direct result of the firing squad coverage.
The law flew through three debates with minimal opposition and passed on Wednesday.
Guatemala is the last country in Central America with a death penalty and the Sept. 13 court-ordered executions of Roberto Giron and Pedro Castillo Mendoza were the first for 13 years.
